source.title_on_document: The impact of AI-assisted composition tools on cultivating creativity among music students in Guangdong province

supplement.where: No supplementary material or appendix is referenced in the document; the PDF ends with transparency, copyright, and references on p. 25.

paper_design_summary: Music students from four institutions in Guangdong completed an AI-assisted composition curriculum or traditional instruction, described as a 12-week intervention with 120 students analyzed, 60 per arm (PDF pp. 5-7, Secs. 3.1-3.3 and Figure 1; p. 15, Table 6). Although the paper calls the study quasi-experimental, its flowchart explicitly says Randomized Assignment and the demographic discussion describes a randomization procedure, so it is coded as a field_rct in real educational settings (PDF pp. 5-7). Experts scored student compositions on nine dimensions and composite scores; AI access while the post-test outputs were produced is not explicitly established (PDF p. 6, Sec. 3.2; pp. 11-12, Table 4; pp. 13-23, results).

studies.label: Music composition curriculum in Guangdong institutions

assignment.what_was_assigned: Students were divided into the AI-assisted composition curriculum and traditional-instruction groups. Figure 1 labels the division Randomized Assignment and shows 60 students per arm. The sequence-generation method, concealment, and any institution-level blocking are not stated; the prose also calls the design quasi-experimental.
assignment.quote: The randomization procedure was effective in creating comparable groups with similar distributions across gender, age, grade level, prior music experience, and primary instrument selection, ensuring valid comparison of intervention effects.
assignment.locator: PDF p. 5 (printed p. 2794), Figure 1, Group Division / Randomized Assignment and arm counts; PDF p. 7 (printed p. 2796), paragraph after Table 1 (quote). Educational setting and conflicting quasi-experimental label: PDF pp. 5-6, Sec. 3.1.
assignment.prereg_locator: No preregistration or registration identifier is stated in the PDF; research methods are on PDF pp. 5-8.

arms.name: AI-assisted composition curriculum
arms.description: Composition instruction with the purpose-built generative AI-Assisted Composition Platform, including melody generation and modification, harmonic generation, structural integration, and culturally informed composition projects (PDF p. 6, Sec. 3.2; p. 9, Table 2; pp. 11-12, Table 4). Assigned arm count: PDF p. 5, Figure 1; analyzed arm count: PDF pp. 13 and 15, Tables 5-6.

arms.name: Traditional composition instruction
arms.description: Traditional composition approaches and instruction during the same intervention period (PDF p. 5, Sec. 3.1 and Figure 1; p. 6, Sec. 3.1). No alternative generative AI tool is specified. Assigned arm count: PDF p. 5, Figure 1; analyzed arm count: PDF pp. 13 and 15, Tables 5-6.

participants.exclusions: No exclusion, attrition, or missing-outcome flow is reported. Figure 1 shows the recruitment/assignment sample and Tables 5-6 retain 60 students per arm; this is not taken as a claim of intention-to-treat analysis. A separate pilot of 28 music students is expressly outside the primary study and is not added to these counts (PDF p. 6, Sec. 3.2).
participants.who: Music students from four institutions offering specialised music programmes in Guangdong; Table 1 lists sophomore, junior, and senior students, age range 17-24 (PDF p. 6, Sec. 3.3; p. 7, Table 1).
participants.country: China (Guangdong Province; PDF pp. 1-2, Introduction, and p. 6, Sec. 3.3).
participants.quote: The primary source of information data was 120 music students from four institutions offering specialised music programmes in Guangdong Province.
participants.locator: PDF p. 6 (printed p. 2795), Sec. 3.3 (quote and recruitment); PDF p. 5, Figure 1 (assignment: n=120, 60 per arm); PDF p. 7, Table 1 (people and demographics); PDF pp. 13 and 15, Tables 5-6 (60 analyzed per arm).

ai_tool.name_model: AI-Assisted Composition Platform (AICP), a purpose-built platform integrating generative artificial neural networks; specific architecture, model version, and vendor not stated (PDF p. 6, Sec. 3.2).
ai_tool.how_used: Interactive music generation and composition assistance: students generated and modified AI-suggested melodies, manipulated AI-generated harmonic progressions, and used form generation, arrangement assistance, and a full composition environment (PDF p. 9, Table 2). This is an educational composition platform rather than a described general chatbot or a fixed set of supplied examples. The formal post-test AI-access protocol is not stated (PDF pp. 6 and 11-12).

task.description: Create and develop original music compositions, including melody, harmony, multi-section musical form, and integration of Guangdong musical traditions; final composition portfolios receive expert evaluation (PDF p. 9, Table 2; pp. 11-12, Table 4; p. 20, Table 7).
task.duration: Described as a 12-week intervention (PDF p. 5, Sec. 3.1; p. 8, Sec. 4.1). Figure 1 places baseline at week 0, intervention in weeks 1-12, and assessment in weeks 13-14 (PDF p. 5); Table 4 instead places preparation in weeks 1-2, modules in weeks 3-12, and synthesis/evaluation in weeks 13-14 (PDF pp. 11-12). Per-composition time limit not stated.

outcomes.name: Overall Creativity
outcomes.measure_detail: Compositional Product Assessment Rubric (CPAR) score on a student composition; scores range from 1 (lowest) to 5 (highest), with five expert evaluators (PDF p. 6, Sec. 3.2; p. 14, Table 5 note; p. 20, Table 7 note). Analysis uses composition-level scores, not individual expert ratings; the complete composition pool is reported as 120 outputs (PDF p. 22, Figure 6 and Sec. 5.5). Tables 5 and 6 report pre/post descriptions and post-test group comparisons, respectively; Figures 2-4 repeat these dimensions (PDF pp. 13-17). Direct expert rating of overall creativity. The paper does not designate a primary outcome; this is the codebook-preferred creativity score. AI was used during the curriculum, and the results describe AI-assisted compositions, but no explicit rule establishes AI availability while the post-test outputs were produced (PDF p. 6, Sec. 3.3; p. 9, Table 2; pp. 11-12, Table 4; p. 18, Sec. 5.3). The question and AI-availability fields are null pending clarification; post-intervention alone does not establish after_ai.
outcomes.delay: Post-intervention assessment is placed in weeks 13-14 after the 12-week intervention in PDF p. 5, Figure 1; final composition development and evaluation are also in weeks 13-14 in PDF p. 12, Table 4. The interval between final AI use, output production, and assessment is not given, so immediate versus delayed is unresolved and no delay in days is inferred.

outcomes.name: Entropy-weighted comprehensive composition score
outcomes.measure_detail: Composite of the expert-rated compositional dimensions, weighted using their variation across student compositions (PDF pp. 21-22, Sec. 5.5, Table 9 and Figure 6). Printed weights from PDF p. 21, Table 9: Cultural Integration: w=0.1652 (16.52%); Creative Fluency: w=0.1547 (15.47%); Expressive Range: w=0.1486 (14.86%); Structural Coherence: w=0.1442 (14.42%); Melodic Originality: w=0.1378 (13.78%); Overall Creativity: w=0.1327 (13.27%); Harmonic Sophistication: w=0.1229 (12.29%); Technical Proficiency: w=0.1103 (11.03%); Rhythmic Complexity: w=0.1016 (10.16%). The continuous score distribution is graphical; no full-sample arm means, SDs, SEs, CIs, or between-group test are supplied for this composite. Rank-block counts and excellence/competence threshold rates are summaries of this same score, kept in this outcome rather than counted as new constructs. These measure assessed quality, not similarity across people. Figure 6 and the accompanying prose disagree on the rank-block composition; both versions are retained. AI was used during the curriculum, and the results describe AI-assisted compositions, but no explicit rule establishes AI availability while the post-test outputs were produced (PDF p. 6, Sec. 3.3; p. 9, Table 2; pp. 11-12, Table 4; p. 18, Sec. 5.3). The question and AI-availability fields are null pending clarification; post-intervention alone does not establish after_ai.

outcomes.name: Average score for representative student compositions
outcomes.measure_detail: Table 7 reports an Average Score column alongside the nine expert-rated dimensions for selected exemplary compositions; the averaging formula is not specified. This descriptive average is listed separately from the directly rated Overall Creativity dimension and the entropy-weighted comprehensive score. The listed outputs are selected examples, not a separate participant sample and not a full-sample effect estimate (PDF p. 18, Sec. 5.3; p. 20, Table 7). The observation count is the number of composition rows in Table 7, not the number of experts or people randomized. None of the form's listed inferential or arm-summary statistics is supplied for this descriptive average. AI was used during the curriculum, and the results describe AI-assisted compositions, but no explicit rule establishes AI availability while the post-test outputs were produced (PDF p. 6, Sec. 3.3; p. 9, Table 2; pp. 11-12, Table 4; p. 18, Sec. 5.3). The question and AI-availability fields are null pending clarification; post-intervention alone does not establish after_ai.

eligibility.reason: The paper explicitly reports randomized assignment of students to AI-assisted composition or traditional instruction (PDF p. 5, Figure 1; p. 7, paragraph after Table 1), despite calling its design quasi-experimental (PDF pp. 1 and 5-6). The platform integrates generative artificial neural networks (PDF p. 6, Sec. 3.2). The analyzed sample is 120 people, 60 per arm (PDF p. 7, Table 1; pp. 13 and 15, Tables 5-6), exceeding the 50-person criterion. Experts score produced compositions on originality and overall creativity, among other dimensions (PDF p. 6, Sec. 3.2; pp. 13 and 15, Tables 5-6; p. 20, Table 7 note). Thus the three screening criteria are met as reported. AI availability while post-test work was produced remains unresolved, so no with_ai versus after_ai classification is forced. Allocation details and the internally inconsistent composite results require audit before extraction or pooling.

one_line_finding: Among 120 analyzed music students (60 per arm), post-test overall creativity was 4.71 (SD 0.54) after the AI-assisted curriculum versus 3.62 (SD 0.69) after traditional instruction, with reported Cohen's d=1.77 and p<.001; post-test AI availability is unspecified (PDF p. 15, Table 6; p. 6, Sec. 3.3; p. 12, Table 4).
open_questions: How was the randomized assignment implemented, and were students allocated individually or through institutional/classroom units? The field_rct/individual coding follows the student flowchart and explicit randomization statement, but the method is unspecified and conflicts with the quasi-experimental label (PDF pp. 5-7).

Were the outputs underlying Tables 5-6 and Figure 6 created with AICP available, or in an unassisted post-test after removal? The curriculum and exemplary compositions are described as AI-assisted, but the production conditions of the formal post-test are not stated (PDF pp. 6, 9, 11-12 and 18-20).

What was the interval between the final AI-assisted activity, production of assessed compositions, and the post-test? Figure 1 and Table 4 place evaluation in weeks 13-14 but do not give that interval; their preparation/intervention schedules also differ (PDF p. 5 and pp. 11-12).

Which rank counts are correct: the labels inside Figure 6 or the different counts in its accompanying prose? The threshold counts are also provided only in the prose, without underlying data (PDF pp. 22-23).

How were the entropy weights normalized and the comprehensive score calculated? The listed proportions do not form a normalized percentage distribution, and no full calculation or underlying scores is supplied (PDF p. 21, Table 9; pp. 22-23, Sec. 5.5).

What are the detailed CPAR anchors, particularly the Creative Fluency and Expressive Range dimensions? The paper supplies expert ratings but no idea or category counts; rater blinding is not stated (PDF p. 6, Sec. 3.2; pp. 13-15; p. 20, Table 7).

Are separate Creativity Assessment Battery subtest results or the stated MANCOVA results available? CAB musical divergent thinking, compositional flexibility, and creative originality are named in methods, but separate results and output-scoring details are not provided; MANCOVA is stated without a results table or coefficients (PDF pp. 6-7, Secs. 3.2 and 3.4; results on pp. 12-23). No supplement is referenced.
notes: All page locators are one-based PDF pages; printed pages run from 2790 to 2814. The entire markdown conversion and all PDF pages were read, and the embedded result figures were inspected without creating image files. Table cells were recovered with PyMuPDF find_tables. Outcome inventory: Tables 5-6 and Figures 2-4 report the same nine CPAR dimensions; Table 7 repeats those dimensions for exemplary works and adds an Average Score column; Table 9 defines entropy weights; Figure 6 reports the entropy-weighted comprehensive score, ranks, and thresholds; Table 10 correlates existing dimensions with that composite and assignment. Eleven output scores are retained, with rank/threshold variants grouped under the composite. The exemplary Average Score is descriptive and must not be treated as a full-sample effect or independent study. Figure 5 reports self-reported composition satisfaction and learning motivation, which are excluded; Table 8 and the regressions in Sec. 5.4 link those questionnaire outcomes with already-listed scores and add no separate eligible output outcome (PDF pp. 18-21). CAB subtests are named without separately reported scores and are documented in open_questions rather than invented as measured output results (PDF p. 6). The separate 28-student instrument pilot has no reported comparative creativity outcomes and is not counted as another study (PDF p. 6). No across-person similarity/homogenization measure is reported; entropy weights describe score variation and do not constitute idea diversity. No preregistered or paper-designated primary outcome is identified; the directly expert-rated Overall Creativity outcome is first under the codebook hierarchy. Null question, AI-availability, and timing fields preserve unresolved production/timing information because the offered categorical choices do not include unknown. No after_ai claim is inferred from the term post-intervention. Reported between-group d values in Table 6 are kept distinct from within-group pre/post d values in Table 5. No effect sizes, SEs, intervals, or pooled quantities were computed. The prose claim about effect sizes in Sec. 5.2 does not agree with the range printed in Table 6, and the quartile labels in Figure 6 contradict its accompanying prose; printed values are retained without correction. Data and code links are not stated.
